title: "w03_Task3"
---

```{r}
library(nycflights13)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
```


Which origin airport is best to minimize my chances of a late arrival when I am using Delta Airlines?

```{r}
delta_flights <- flights %>%
  filter(carrier == "DL") %>%
  filter(!is.na(arr_delay)) %>%
  mutate(late_15 = arr_delay > 15)
```

```{r}
origin_summary <- delta_flights %>%
  group_by(origin) %>%
  summarize(total_flights = n(),
    avg_arrival_delay = mean(arr_delay),
    median_arrival_delay = median(arr_delay),
    percent_late_15 = mean(late_15),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(percent_late_15)

origin_summary
```

```{r}
ggplot(origin_summary, aes(x = reorder(origin, percent_late_15), y = percent_late_15)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Percent of Delta Flights Arriving More Than 15 Minutes Late",
    y = "Percent")
```

```{r}
ggplot(delta_flights, aes(x = origin, y = arr_delay)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.15, width = 0.2) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.3, outlier.shape = NA) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-75, 200)) +
  labs(title = "Individual Delta Flight Arrival Delays by Origin Airport",
    y = "Delay in Minutes")
```

```{r}
best_origin <- origin_summary %>%
  slice_min(percent_late_15, n = 1)

best_origin
```

The JFK airport has the best chance to minimize a late arrival while using Delta. On average Delta overestimates their arrival delay from JFK to anywhere so they let their passengers feel like they are getting in early. This doesn't necessarily mean that they arrive faster but that they give a generous gap for their pilots to work with in getting from point A to point B.







Which destination airport is the worst airport for arrival delays? You decide on the metric for “worst.”

```{r destination-summary}
destination_summary <- delta_flights %>%
  group_by(dest) %>%
  summarize(total_flights = n(),
    avg_arrival_delay = mean(arr_delay),
    median_arrival_delay = median(arr_delay),
    percent_late_15 = mean(late_15),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(total_flights >= 30) %>%
  arrange(desc(percent_late_15))

destination_summary
```

```{r worst-destination-chart}
destination_summary %>%
  slice_max(percent_late_15, n = 10) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(dest, percent_late_15), y = percent_late_15)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Worst Delta Destination Airports for Arrival Delays",
    y = "Percent")
```

```{r worst-destination-answer}
worst_destination <- destination_summary %>%
  slice_max(percent_late_15, n = 1)

worst_destination
```

The worst airport for arrival delays would be SAT. This is because the average arrival delay is the highest out of all of the other airports, the median delay is one of the top 3 and the percent of flights that get delayed is the highest out of all of them.
